svg.title: Row 7 of countdown.c scanned left to right by editorUpdateSyntax at 06.02: the class each character gets, and the two things the scan keeps as it goes
svg.text: row 7, as render holds it: the tab is 8 spaces. One box per byte of render; under it, its class in hl
the scan's state after the characters in the box

g.title: Spaces at the start, here the tab's 8, are skipped and stay normal (class 0). prev_sep starts at 1: a word may start at the first character.
"char": no quote, no digit, no separator. Normal, and prev_sep = 0: each letter after the first is inside a word.
' ': separator, so normal, and prev_sep = 1: a word may start after it.
"order": a word again, normal. This lesson has no keywords: a word is never coloured.
'[': separator, so normal, and prev_sep = 1: a word may start after it.
'1' is a digit and prev_sep is 1: a number starts here. Class 7, HL_NUMBER, red.
'0' is a digit right after a number (the class before it is 7): the number goes on.
"] = ": separators, so normal, and prev_sep = 1: a word may start after them.
A double quote opens a string: in_string holds the quote that will close it. The quote itself is class 6, HL_STRING, magenta.
g.text: inside a string that a " closes

g.title: "lift off!": inside a string every character is string, the space and the ! too. The scan only looks for the closing quote, or a backslash.
g.text: inside a string that a " closes

g.title: The same quote again: it is string too, and it closes the string (in_string = 0).
';': separator, so normal, and prev_sep = 1: a word may start after it. The end of render: the row is done.
